description_full: Pan American Silver Corp. engages in the exploration, mine development, extraction, processing, refining, and reclamation of mines in Chile, Peru, Brazil, Mexico, Canada, Argentina, Bolivia, and Guatemala. The Silver segment includes the La Colorada, Juanicipio, Cerro Moro, Huaron, and San Vicente mines. The Gold segment comprises the Jacobina, El Peñon, Timmins, Shahuindo, Minera Florida, and Dolores mines. It explores silver, gold, zinc, lead, and copper deposits. The company was formerly known as Pan American Minerals Corp. and changed its name to Pan American Silver Corp. in April 1995. Pan American Silver Corp. was incorporated in 1979 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.

Each employee generates $109K of free cash flow annually. CEO compensation is 8× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (8/10).
financial_summary: Pan American Silver Corp. is a large-cap basic materials business with a $17.0B market cap on $3.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +34% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 6% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 19% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $1.0B in free cash flow — roughly 28 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.36× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 1.3%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
